subject: Human Evolution
title: Back Pain's Deep Roots
description: A quick, practical guide to Back Pain's Deep Roots.

hook.text: 80% of adults will experience lower back pain. It's not a modern problem—it's an evolutionary one.

buildup.text: Our spine was originally a horizontal beam. Evolution bent it vertical, stacking vertebrae like blocks.

discovery.text: The lumbar curve that keeps us upright also concentrates stress on a few vulnerable lower discs.

twist.text: People whose vertebrae most resemble chimp shapes are most likely to suffer disc herniation.

climax.text: Back pain is the price we pay for the bipedal posture that made us human.

punchline.text: We traded a horizontal beam for a vertical stack.

quiz.question: Why is lower back pain so common in humans?
options: Our spine was adapted from a horizontal to vertical design
Our bones are weaker than other primates
